name: Albanian Tavë Kosi
description: Tavë kosi, Albania's real national dish, means literally 'yogurt baking dish' - real technique doesn't just pour yogurt over the lamb, it stabilizes the yogurt and egg with a real butter-flour roux whisked in first, which is what lets the topping bake into a thick, puffed, soufflé-like custard instead of curdling or weeping in the oven.
steps_detailed: Brown the lamb with the garlic and oregano in half the butter, 8-9 minutes.
Add 1.25 cups water, bring to a boil, then reduce and simmer 25-30 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Remove the lamb, add the rice to the broth, and cook until tender, about 15 minutes; combine with the lamb in a baking dish.
Melt the remaining butter in a small pan, whisk in the flour, and cook 1-2 minutes into a real roux.
Whisk the eggs into the yogurt, then whisk in the warm roux until smooth.
Pour the yogurt mixture over the lamb and rice, and bake at 375F (190C) for 30-35 minutes, until puffed and deeply golden on top.

name: Albanian Byrek
description: Byrek, a flaky savory pie with layered phyllo, is a genuine Albanian staple eaten at any meal, real versions cooking the spinach filling until any released liquid fully evaporates, so the pastry doesn't turn soggy.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion and garlic in the olive oil, 3-4 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook, stirring, until wilted and any released liquid has fully evaporated, 5-7 minutes - real technique depends on this to keep the pastry crisp.
Let cool slightly, then mix in the feta and beaten egg.
Layer the phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil, spread the filling, and roll or fold into a spiral or layered pie.
Bake at 375F (190C) for 25-28 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Albanian Fërgesë
description: Fërgesë, roasted peppers and tomatoes combined with real cottage cheese, is a beloved Albanian comfort dish - real technique roasts the peppers until genuinely charred and blistered first, not just softened in a pan, which is what builds the dish's real smoky depth; the summer version uses cheese alone, while a winter version traditionally adds real meat, often liver.
steps_detailed: Roast the bell pepper at 450F (230C) for 20-25 minutes, turning once, until the skin is genuinely charred and blistered - this real roasting, not just softening in a pan, is what builds fërgesë's smoky depth.
Let cool slightly, peel off the charred skin, and chop.
Cook the garlic in the olive oil, 30 seconds, then add the roasted pepper and tomatoes, and simmer 10-12 minutes until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in the cottage cheese, so it doesn't overcook and turn rubbery.

name: Albanian Tarator
description: Tarator, a cold cucumber and yogurt soup, is a refreshing Albanian summer staple, shared across the wider Balkans, real technique salting the cucumber first to draw out excess water.
steps_detailed: Salt the grated cucumber and let sit 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess water.
Whisk the yogurt with the garlic and olive oil, then stir in the cucumber and mint.
Chill at least 20 minutes before serving.

name: Albanian Qofte
description: Qofte, grilled meat patties, is a beloved Albanian street food, real technique grates the onion on a box grater and includes its released juices in the mix, then rests the whole mixture in the fridge at least an hour, not just a quick 15 minutes, so the flavors genuinely meld before shaping.
steps_detailed: Mix the beef with the grated onion (including its juice), cumin, mint, and garlic, folding gently just until combined - real technique avoids overmixing, which toughens the meat.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour, so the flavors genuinely meld.
Shape into small oval patties.
Grill or pan-sear, 4-5 minutes per side, until well charred and cooked through.

name: Albanian Speca Të Mbushur (Stuffed Peppers)
description: Speca të mbushur, peppers stuffed with rice and meat, is a genuine Albanian home-cooking staple, real technique par-cooking the rice first so it finishes tender inside the pepper without drying it out.
steps_detailed: Par-cook the rice about 10 minutes, until just short of tender.
Mix the beef, par-cooked rice, and onion together.
Stuff the mixture into the peppers, stand them in a baking dish, and pour the tomatoes around and over.
Bake at 375F (190C) for 35-40 minutes until the peppers are tender and the filling is cooked through.

name: Albanian Baklava
description: Baklava, layered phyllo with real chopped walnuts and honey syrup, reflects genuine Ottoman influence found throughout Albanian sweets.
steps_detailed: Layer half the phyllo sheets in a baking dish, brushing each with melted butter.
Scatter the walnuts evenly over the top.
Layer the remaining phyllo sheets over the nuts, brushing each with butter, and cut into diamond shapes before baking.
Bake at 325F (165C) for 30-35 minutes until deeply golden.
Warm the honey with the sugar and a splash of water, and pour over the hot baklava immediately.

name: Albanian Roasted Peppers (Speca Të Pjekur)
description: Roasted red peppers dressed simply with olive oil and garlic are a beloved Albanian side, real technique charring the skin fully so it peels away cleanly.
steps_detailed: Roast the peppers at 450F (230C) for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until the skin is fully charred and blistered.
Let cool slightly, then peel off the skin and slice.
Toss with the garlic and olive oil.
